## Summing a warp

The two atomic routes leave the total in memory rather than in a register, so
their answer accumulates across the block's warps where the other two do not.
That is the reason to reach for one, and the cycles are the price.

| Warps | Route | Instructions | Warp steps | Lane ops | Cycles |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | shared | 68 | 68 | 2176 | 354 |
| 1 | shuffle | 33 | 33 | 1056 | 149 |
| 1 | atomic a lane | 5 | 5 | 160 | 1143 |
| 1 | shuffle+atomic | 39 | 39 | 1155 | 363 |
| 2 | shared | 68 | 136 | 4352 | 370 |
| 2 | shuffle | 33 | 66 | 2112 | 150 |
| 2 | atomic a lane | 5 | 10 | 320 | 1144 |
| 2 | shuffle+atomic | 39 | 78 | 2310 | 366 |
| 4 | shared | 68 | 272 | 8704 | 402 |
| 4 | shuffle | 33 | 132 | 4224 | 152 |
| 4 | atomic a lane | 5 | 20 | 640 | 1146 |
| 4 | shuffle+atomic | 39 | 156 | 4620 | 372 |
| 8 | shared | 68 | 544 | 17408 | 654 |
| 8 | shuffle | 33 | 264 | 8448 | 264 |
| 8 | atomic a lane | 5 | 40 | 1280 | 1162 |
| 8 | shuffle+atomic | 39 | 312 | 9240 | 504 |

Priced at 8, a shuffle would have to reach 22 before shared memory and the
exchange came level.

One warp: an atomic a lane is 5 instructions against 39 and 1143 cycles
against 363. The issue count says it wins and the clock says it loses by
3.1x — thirty-two lanes on one address are thirty-two operations, worked
through one at a time.
